review.judge_objection: Against: a riverside lawn and playgrounds used by locals; it is the view rather than the park that is the draw. If kept, name it South Perth Foreshore and check it is not the same place as another candidate (the Old Mill and Perth Zoo are on the same foreshore).

review.name: Yellagonga Regional Park
review.case_for: For: the DBCA visitor page (managing agency) describes Lake Joondalup and Lake Goollelal with walking and cycling circuits, birdlife and settler-era ruins.
review.judge_objection: Against: DBCA writes a page for every regional park; it is suburban parkland that DBCA itself calls 'a leafy oasis in the heart of suburbia', and no guide names it (close to the 'regional park beside a city that no guide mentions' rule).

review.name: Rockingham Lakes Regional Park
review.case_for: For: the DBCA page names two real draws, the Lake Richmond thrombolites ('a star attraction of the park') and Cape Peron, its hub, with snorkelling, viewing platforms and a coastal walk.
review.judge_objection: Against: an umbrella area; its draws are better judged as places of their own (Cape Peron, Lake Richmond), and a park-wide pin would duplicate them.

review.name: West Australian Reptile Park
review.case_for: For: the Swan Valley's tourism site lists it (pythons, venomous snakes, crocodiles, wombats and dingoes, with presentations) at Henley Brook. Rule 2: paid wildlife park.
review.judge_objection: Against: one counted source for a small private park, and Caversham Wildlife Park nearby covers the same wildlife-park draw better.

review.name: Kanyana Wildlife Rehabilitation Centre
review.case_for: For: Experience Perth Hills names it among the hills' 10 must-visit wildlife experiences (Discovery Tours, nocturnal tours; bilbies and woylies); Destination Perth listed it. Against rule 2: it is a working wildlife hospital visitors can enter only on booked tours on Thursdays and Sundays, not whenever they arrive.
review.judge_objection: Tour-only access two days a week, bookings essential; one counted source for a marginal place.

review.name: Peninsula Farm
review.case_for: For: the National Trust heritage house and farm (formerly Tranby House, now 'Peninsula Farm at Wu-rut Woorat', 1839) on the Swan River; Hello Perth visitor guide names it, the house is open with volunteer guides and an entry fee, the grounds daily, with a cafe. Likely the same place as any 'Tranby House' candidate: keep as one under its current name.
review.judge_objection: The house opens only Friday and Saturday; one visitor source; a suburban heritage house museum, 'only if nearby'.

review.name: Cantonment Hill
review.case_for: For: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing ('a terrific view of Fremantle Harbour'), free lookout beside the Army Museum. Against: one counted source and a short viewpoint visit; the signal station building is not open; Visit Fremantle points visitors to Monument Hill instead.
review.judge_objection: Marginal per the one-source-and-short-visit rule; may be best mentioned in the Army Museum's bio.

review.name: The Moores Building
review.case_for: For: Wikivoyage Do listing: a contemporary art gallery with six exhibition spaces in the West End, free entry. Against rule 3: Wikivoyage itself calls it part of Fremantle Arts Centre; a small gallery whose shows come and go.
review.judge_objection: Part-of signal: if Fremantle Arts Centre is kept, this is a near-duplicate; could also be folded into the West End spot.

review.name: Cappuccino Strip
review.case_for: For: Fremantle's famous cafe street (South Terrace), named by Wikivoyage (walking area), Visit Fremantle ('the famous Cappuccino Strip', a stop on the Fremantle Discovery Trail) and Tourism WA. Against rule 2: it is a strip of cafes and restaurants; a street of businesses, which the bar fails unless the street itself is the recognised attraction.
review.judge_objection: Could be judged a recognised landmark street (keep) or folded into a Fremantle town/West End spot.

review.name: Esplanade Park, Fremantle
review.case_for: For: Tourism WA's Fremantle page (Ferris wheel at Esplanade Park) and Visit Fremantle (Esplanade Reserve on the Discovery Trail, skate park, playground). Against rule 3 / Leave out: an urban park under Norfolk pines whose draws are a seasonal-ish tourist wheel and a youth skate park; 'an ordinary park' negative benchmark.
review.judge_objection: Two counted sources name it, but as a place to pass through on the way to the Fishing Boat Harbour.

review.name: Armstrong Bay
review.case_for: For: (Little) Armstrong Bay is repeatedly named by Rottnest guides as one of the island's best beginner snorkelling bays. Against: sources found are ferry operators, not counted; one of dozens of Rottnest bays; the candidate is 'Armstrong Bay' while guides name 'Little Armstrong Bay'.
review.judge_objection: Rottnest has 60+ bays; listing many dilutes the island; one beach spot (The Basin) may suffice.

review.name: Thomson Bay
review.case_for: For: the island's main settlement where the ferries land, with the shops, bakery, museum and accommodation; visitors base there (town rule). Against rule 3: it is the arrival point of Rottnest Island rather than a separate draw, and no counted source names it as somewhere to go in itself.
review.judge_objection: Likely a near-duplicate of Rottnest Island; useful only if the island becomes a destination with the settlement as its gateway spot.

review.name: All Saints Anglican Church, Henley Brook
review.case_for: For: Wikivoyage Swan Valley See listing names it as Western Australia's oldest church (1841) with a historic cemetery, grounds and a walk to the Swan River; entry free (church rule: a landmark a guide singles out). Against: one counted source and a short visit; still a working parish church.
review.judge_objection: One source plus a 20-30 minute stop; marginal by rule.

review.name: Rocky Pool
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills mentions Rocky Pool in Swan View as a start of the Railway Reserves Heritage Trail; DBCA Kalamunda National Park lists a "Rocky Pool" attraction (on Piesse Brook). Case for: a natural swimming hole named by two sources.
review.judge_objection: The two sources may be two different Rocky Pools (Swan View/John Forrest vs Kalamunda NP); the Wikivoyage mention is only a trail access point, not a listing. Confirm which one and its coordinates before keeping.

review.name: Goat Farm Mountain Bike Park
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Perth/The Hills (Do: mountain biking) names it; Trails WA carries it as a trail (Greenmount). Case for: a real open-access mountain bike park in the hills.
review.judge_objection: Mostly used by local riders who bring their own bikes; a passing mention in one counted source; closer to "a place only locals use" than a visitor draw.

review.name: Helena National Park
review.case_for: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page (jarrah and wandoo forest, Bibbulmun Track). Case for: a national park with a visitor page and a road-access lookout.
review.judge_objection: Its only named draw is Mount Dale, a separate candidate; without it the park is unmarked bush with no facilities. Keep one (Mount Dale) unless the park has another visitor point.

review.name: Kalamunda National Park
review.case_for: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page; the Bibbulmun Track northern terminus and Piesse Brook walks start here. Case for: the start of WA's best-known long walk.
review.judge_objection: No facilities; the draw is the Bibbulmun Track (a separate candidate) and the terminus in Kalamunda town. Near-duplicate of Bibbulmun Track and Kalamunda.

review.name: Mandurah Museum
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Mandurah See listing only ("small local history museum", gold-coin donation). Case for: open to the public, about an hour.
review.judge_objection: One counted source, a small local museum; fails the friend test unless already in Mandurah.

review.name: Amaze Miniature Park
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Mandurah See listing (Wed-Sat 10-4:30). Case for: a family attraction a guide names.
review.judge_objection: One counted source with a one-word description; opens four days a week; a local family attraction.

review.name: Mandjar Bay
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Mandurah names Mandjar Bay as the base for dolphin tours; Visit Mandurah lists it as one of the best places to see dolphins. Case for: dolphins are seen from the shore here, on the town's waterfront.
review.judge_objection: It is Mandurah's foreshore and marina where tours leave from (a tour base, not a draw of its own), so it may be a near-duplicate of Mandurah itself.

review.name: Captain Fawcett 4WD Trail
review.case_for: Rule 1: DBCA site page (four-wheel-drive track through jarrah forest) and Trails WA (40 km, Dwellingup to Quindanning). Case for: a named agency-promoted route.
review.judge_objection: Only for experienced 4WD drivers with their own vehicle; Trails WA says it is currently impassable and closed for winter; a vehicle route rather than a place most visitors go.

review.name: Waroona
review.case_for: Town rule: Destination Perth has a Shire of Waroona page, but its draws are Waroona Dam, Drakesbrook Weir, Lane Poole, Yalgorup and Preston Beach, not the town; the town gets only "experience the charm of Waroona's town centre" and a visitor centre with a gallery. Case for: a highway town with a visitor centre.
review.judge_objection: A shire page, not the town: a town with nothing of its own named to see. Waroona Dam or Drakesbrook Weir may be the real candidates.

review.name: Mandurah Hill
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Rockingham See listing only ("wonderful look out with excellent views", Golden Bay). Case for: a free lookout a guide names.
review.judge_objection: One counted source, a suburban dune lookout with a short visit; no tourism board mention found.

review.name: Shoalwater Islands Marine Park
review.case_for: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page (snorkelling, dive wreck, kayak tours to Seal Island with sea lions, boardwalks) and Destination Perth Rockingham page. Case for: two counted sources and a real range of water activities.
review.judge_objection: Rule 3: an area containing Penguin Island, Seal Island and Point Peron, which are separate spots; much of what it offers is tours. Better as the context in those bios than as its own spot.

review.name: Marmion Marine Park
review.case_for: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page (reefs, Boyinaboat Reef dive trail off Hillarys, Mettam's Pool, whale watching). Case for: a named marine park with shore-access diving.
review.judge_objection: Rule 3: an area whose visitor points are Mettam's Pool and Hillarys Boat Harbour, which are separate candidates; most of it needs a boat or charter.

review.name: Strickland Bay
review.case_for: Rule 1: Destination Perth names it only in a list of surf spots (Rottnest Island's main surf break). Case for: a named bay on Rottnest that surfers go to.
review.judge_objection: A passing mention in a surf list; Wikivoyage Rottnest Island does not name it; one of many Rottnest bays and a ride from the settlement.

review.name: Floreat Beach
review.case_for: Rule 1: Destination Perth's 'Best Beaches in Perth' names it among the Sunset Coast beaches and Tourism WA's City Beach page mentions the promenade linking to it; a patrolled swimming beach.
review.judge_objection: Rule 3: it adjoins City Beach on one promenade and is only ever named in passing beside it; likely a near-duplicate of City Beach.

review.name: North Beach
review.case_for: Rule 1: Destination Perth's beaches guide names North Beach in its Sunset Coast list; an open beach on the coastal path.
review.judge_objection: Named only in a list, with nothing said about it; one weak counted source for a suburban beach near better-known Trigg and Scarborough.

review.name: C.Y. O'Connor Beach
review.case_for: Rule 1: Destination Perth's Fremantle beaches guide names O'Connor Reserve as a dog-friendly beach; the beach is known for the C.Y. O'Connor statue standing in the water.
review.judge_objection: Rule 1: the mention is a passing one for a dog beach; no counted source describes the statue or the beach as a place to go. Mainly local use.

review.name: Bicton Baths
review.case_for: Rule 1+2: DBCA Explore Parks has a site page (Swan Canning Riverpark) for swimming, canoeing and walking at this 1926 river baths; free, open access.
review.judge_objection: Rule 'places only locals use': a neighbourhood river swimming spot with one agency page and no tourism-board listing.

review.name: York Suspension Bridge
review.case_for: Rule 1+3: Wikivoyage York See listing and Destination Perth's Avon Valley road trip ('cross the river by suspension bridge'); a footbridge over the Avon by Holy Trinity.
review.judge_objection: Rule 3: a few minutes' walk across, and it is a 1988 rebuild; better as part of York town's bio than a spot of its own.

review.name: Avon Terrace
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage York names the main street lined with 19th-century buildings, and Destination Perth's York page describes its heritage streetscape and walking trails.
review.judge_objection: Rule 3: it is York's town centre itself; if York is listed (as a town or destination) this is a near-duplicate and belongs in York's description.

review.name: Pelham Reserve
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Toodyay See listing (wooded hill, Drummond memorial, WWI range, WWII bunker) and Destination Perth's Toodyay page and road trip (spring wildflowers, stargazing over town).
review.judge_objection: Leave-out rule: an ordinary town reserve with picnic sites; mainly a local park, seasonally interesting for wildflowers.

review.name: Northam Heritage Forum
review.case_for: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Northam See listing (old locomotives in a disused railway station, Fri-Mon 11-3).
review.judge_objection: One counted source, a one-line listing; limited opening days; a small volunteer railway museum.

review.name: Mount Ommanney Lookout
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Northam See listing (lookout reached by road or a hike).
review.judge_objection: One counted source and a one-line mention; no tourism-board page found; a short-stop town lookout.

review.name: Yonderup Cave
review.case_for: Rule 1: DBCA Yanchep page names it as a guided-tour cave alongside Crystal Cave.
review.judge_objection: Rule 3: a second cave in the same park, toured less often than Crystal Cave; likely a near-duplicate of the Crystal Cave spot.

review.name: Matilda Bay
review.case_for: Rule 1: DBCA's 'Enjoy nature in Perth' says to relax at Matilda Bay Reserve, grassy riverside parkland facing Perth city and Kings Park.
review.judge_objection: One counted source, a passing mention; a riverside picnic reserve that locals use more than visitors; near Kings Park.

review.name: London Court
review.case_for: Rule 1: Visit Perth (City of Perth) lists it as a 1937 Tudor-style heritage arcade; Tourism WA lists laneway walking tours that feature it.
review.judge_objection: Rule 2: it is a shopping arcade, which the rule fails as a shop venue; it is a quick photo stop on the way between Hay Street Mall and St Georges Terrace.

review.name: Herdsman Lake
review.case_for: Rule 1+2: DBCA park page for Herdsman Lake Regional Park (birdwatching wetland, Discovery Centre, walk and cycle trails), free.
review.judge_objection: Leave-out rule: an urban wetland park mainly used by local walkers and birders; one agency source, no tourism-board listing found.

review.name: Claisebrook Cove
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Perth/City See listing ('spend an hour or so wandering' the architecture; footbridge views of the city at night).
review.judge_objection: One counted source; an urban redevelopment and dining precinct that few visitor sources treat as a sight.
